headline: Sales beat guidance, spin-off complete, EPS hit by costs
summary_short: Middleby's Q2 2026 net sales rose 9.9% y/y to $875.5M (6.4% organic) and Adjusted EBITDA grew 6.4% to $193.2M, but GAAP diluted EPS fell 39.2% y/y to $1.21 on transaction and financing costs tied to the completed spin-off of its Food Processing business into Midera.
summary_long: Q2 2026 net sales grew 9.9% y/y to $875.5M (6.4% organic, 8.3% in Commercial Foodservice), beating the high end of guidance. Adjusted EBITDA rose 6.4% to $193.2M and Adjusted diluted EPS rose 6.8% to $2.35, aided by organic growth, buybacks, and a discrete FX benefit, partly offset by higher interest costs and taxes. GAAP operating income was flat at $147.7M after $14.5M of spin-related transaction costs; GAAP diluted EPS fell 39.2% to $1.21 on a $28.9M equity-in-losses charge plus those costs and a $4.6M tax item. Middleby completed the Food Processing spin-off (Midera) July 6 and raised FY2026 Commercial Foodservice revenue-growth guidance to +6-8%. Net debt was $1.8B, 2.4x leverage.
confidence_notes: REGENERATED (force-regenerate mode): this run was explicitly executed in force-regenerate mode per instructions to overwrite the file at data/summaries/MIDD_US_FY2026_Q2.json; the resolver in fact reported summaryExists=false, so this happens to be a fresh compose rather than a literal overwrite, but the run was still dispatched and executed under the force-regen directive. Basis-mismatch note on the headline GAAP EPS figures: the release's own bullet cites 'Diluted GAAP EPS of $1.20 as compared to $1.91 in prior year' -- those are CONTINUING-OPERATIONS-ONLY figures. This summary's 'Diluted EPS (GAAP)' KPI row instead uses the shard's eps_diluted_usd field ($1.21 vs prior-year $1.99), which is the company's TOTAL diluted EPS including discontinued operations (continuing $1.20 + discontinued $0.01 = $1.21; prior year continuing $1.91 + discontinued $0.08 = $1.99), so the two figures are not directly comparable to the release's headline bullet -- both are legitimate GAAP numbers, just different scopes. Net income, cash, long-term debt, and shareholders' equity all show large y/y swings (net income -48.3%, cash -68.9%, equity -39.0%) driven by the Food Processing/Residential portfolio transformation (partial divestiture of Residential Kitchen Equipment Group for ~$564.6M of six-month proceeds, a $28.9M equity-in-losses-of-affiliate charge on the resulting investment, and heavy buyback activity -- 8.7M shares / 16% of shares outstanding repurchased over the past six quarters) rather than core operating deterioration; treat these balance-sheet deltas as structurally distorted by the spin, not read-through to ongoing profitability. The Food Processing spin-off itself (creating Midera) legally completed July 6, 2026 -- three days after this Q2 report's period end (July 4, 2026) -- so the Q2 continuing-operations figures still include Food Processing per the release's own framing ('All results reflect Food Processing as continuing operations... given reporting... under discontinued operations will be reflected starting in Q3 2026'); FY2026 guidance issued in this release is presented on a POST-spin, ex-Food-Processing, ex-Residential basis and is therefore not directly comparable in scope to the Q2 actuals reported alongside it. Adjusted EPS excluding Food Processing ($1.74) is explicitly labeled by the company as a preliminary estimate subject to finalization once discontinued-operations accounting is completed in Q3 2026.

drivers.explanation: CEO Tim FitzGerald: the quarter "marked a transformational milestone" with the Food Processing separation completed and Midera launched, leaving Middleby "a pure-play commercial foodservice company."
9.9% reported / 6.4% organic growth; Commercial Foodservice organic growth of 8.3% was "broad-based across channels, customer types, and regions" per the CEO.

Company states growth "includes an increase related to organic growth, benefits from share repurchases and a discrete benefit" tied to FX from the spin, partly offset by higher interest costs from the convertible-notes maturity and a higher tax rate.
Flat y/y despite higher sales because the quarter includes $14.5M of strategic transaction costs tied to the Food Processing/Residential portfolio transformation.

Reconciliation table attributes the decline to a $28.9M equity-in-losses-of-affiliate charge, $14.5M strategic transaction costs, and a $4.6M discrete tax impact from the spin, only partly offset by fewer diluted shares outstanding.
Derived from the cash-flow statement: $99.7M of quarterly operating cash flow was more than offset by $102.8M used in financing activities (buybacks) and $11.6M used in investing.

Not itemized by component in the release; the y/y decline coincides with heavy buyback activity (8.7M shares, 16% of shares outstanding repurchased over six quarters) and the Residential/Food Processing portfolio actions.
